newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds up on softer interbank.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds up on softer interbank.

text.p: Singapore government bonds ended higher on Friday in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, in line with a softer interbank rate, dealers said.
"Bond prices were marked up slightly today following a small fall in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.60/98.65 compared with Thursday's close of S$98.55/98.65, May 2002 at S$99.55/99.60 against S$99.43/99.53 and June 2003 at S$94.58/94.63 from S$94.46/94.56.
The overnight interbank offered rate fell to 2 1-7/8 percent versus Thursday's 2-3/4 2-5/8 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.65/2.60 percent against Thursday's yield of 2.93/2.88 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.63/2.58 percent from 2.73/2.68 percent.
